### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description


Sometimes, when navigating completion items, too much text is inserted. This can be confusing.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

```lua

---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
local function setup_deps(path_to_site)
  local mini_path = path_to_site .. "pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
  if not vim.uv.fs_stat(mini_path) then
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    vim.fn.system({ "git", "clone", "--filter=blob:none", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path })
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim | helptags ALL")
    vim.cmd('echo "Installed `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
  end
  require("mini.deps").setup({ path = { package = path_to_site } })
end

local function setup_native_autocompletion()
  vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("LspAttach", {
    group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("my.lsp", {}),
    callback = function(args)
      local client = assert(vim.lsp.get_client_by_id(args.data.client_id))
      if client:supports_method("textDocument/completion") then
        local chars = {} -- optional: trigger autocompletion on EVERY keypress. May be slow!
        -- stylua: ignore
        -- for i = 32, 126 do table.insert(chars, string.char(i)) end
        -- client.server_capabilities.completionProvider.triggerCharacters = chars
        vim.lsp.completion.enable(true, client.id, args.buf, { autotrigger = true })
      end
    end,
  })
end

local function setup_mini_autocompletion()
  require("mini.snippets").setup() -- only using lsp snippets...
  require("mini.completion").setup({ lsp_completion = { auto_setup = false, source_func = "omnifunc" } })
end

local function custom_on_attach(_, bufnr) vim.bo[bufnr].omnifunc = "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp" end

local use_mini = true
vim.g.mapleader = " "
vim.o.shortmess = "CFOSWaco"
vim.o.completeopt = "menuone,noselect,fuzzy"

setup_deps(vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/")
MiniDeps.now(function()
  require("mini.icons").setup()
  MiniIcons.tweak_lsp_kind()
  MiniDeps.add({ source = "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter", checkout = "master" })
  require("nvim-treesitter.configs").setup({ ensure_installed = { "rust" } })

  if use_mini then
    setup_mini_autocompletion()
  else
    setup_native_autocompletion()
  end

  MiniDeps.add("neovim/nvim-lspconfig")
  require("lspconfig").rust_analyzer.setup({ -- have rust-analyzer installed...
    on_attach = use_mini and custom_on_attach or nil,
  })
end)

```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b1b29b2-3dcb-4544-8473-34c02be9faaf

<details>

<summary>Rust testfile</summary>

```rs

fn main() {
    let v = vec![1, 2, 3];
    let v2 = 
}

```

</details>

1 Position cursor after `let v2 = `
2 Enter `v.iter().rev`
3 Enter `ctrl-n` to select `rev`
4 Notice that the text now becomes `let v2 = revreverse`

Repeat with builtin completion (or `blink.cmp`), and notice that in step 4 the text is `let v2 = rev`.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

I could indeed reproduce issue with 'mini.completion' and no issue with `vim.lsp.completion`. With a caveat that accepting item in 'mini.completion' results in correctly inserted `rev()` snippet.

The reason this happens is because `rust-analyzer` returns `revrevision` as `filterText`:

```lua
  -- ...
  filterText = "revreverse",
  insertTextFormat = 2,
  kind = 2,
  label = "rev()",
  -- ...
  textEdit = {
    -- ...
    newText = "rev()$0",
    -- ...
  }
```

As 'mini.completion' prefers to use `filterText` as `word` field of complete-item (after 9af69d8c655e609a7eb043e8f9c27530580d4838 for reasons described in the commit, which resolved #1721), it uses `revrevision` in this case. My guess would be that `rust-analyzer` itself wants to have a "feature" that typing `reverse` would still match the `rev()` item, which *does* happen in 'mini.completion'. There are couple of other instances of this behavior:
- `filterText = "rfoldfoldr"` for `rfold(${1:init}, ${2:f})$0` snippet.
- `filterText = "skip_whiledrop_while"` for `skip_while(${1:predicate})$0` snippet.

As built-in popup-menu doesn't have the distinction between "text to be inserted after `<C-n>` / `<C-p>`" and "text used for filtering" (both use `word`), this is a necessary side effect to ensure filtering that LSP server intends to do.

Closing as "working as expected and limited to the upstream Neovim/Vim capabilities".

---

The `vim.lsp.completion` uses `item.label` here for `word` instead of `item.filterText` (after [this commit](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/b9e6fa7ec81c463d77cc919392b52f6df2d8d304)). This in itself doesn't fully support the idea of "aliases" in `filterText`. Coincidentally, this does work *in this particular case* because `rust-analyzer` seems to always set `isIncomplete = true` so that candidates are re-evaluated after every keystroke. So after typing `reve`, the `rev()` item would still match, but pressing `<C-n>` now inserts `revreverse`. My guess would be that if there were `isIncomplete = false`, then `vim.lsp.completion` wouldn't support these aliases because complete-item would still have `rev` as its `word` (and thus not matching `reve`  prefix).

There is also an effect of `vim.lsp.completion` not supporting/advertising support for `labelDetails`. This results in explicit `rev()(alias reverse) (as Iterator)` supplied as `item.label`. While 'mini.completion' does support/advertise `labelDetails` and `(alias reverse) (as Iterator)` is returned as `item.labelDetails.detail`. Not sure if this makes a difference.

I didn't check 'blink.cmp', but my guess is that it uses `item.filterText` for filtering and `item.label` to show as label, i.e. doesn't have constraints of popup-menu.

Thanks for the explanation!

I am using `vim.o.completeopt = "menuone,noselect,fuzzy"`.

Are there any drawbacks to changing `noselect` into `noinsert`? I vaguely remember you having an opinion on `noinsert` that I can't find anymore.

I tested the setting and it seems to work fine. I can type `rev<c-y>` without having to first select `rev` with `<c-n>`.
When `noinsert` is active the documentation window always pops up. For me that is acceptable.

> Are there any drawbacks to changing `noselect` into `noinsert`? I vaguely remember you having an opinion on `noinsert` that I can't find anymore.

My reservations were that this basically changes "opt-in" style of accepting into "opt-out". I thought that this would have effect in case when the first item is snippet item and typing past that would insert the snippet. But just trying it out now, it doesn't seem to be the case. It seems that `v:completed_item` is empty in that case and is non-empty only if user explicitly selected an item.

Not sure if there are other drawbacks. Except maybe having very visible line from pmenu on every completion.
Thanks! I am going to use it for a while. In conjunction with `fuzzy` it seems really useful.

title: [mini.completion] Sometimes too much text is inserted on ctrl-n
